nodes.evidence: FuzzPath is present on the observed crash stack (frame #2 at FuzzCommon.cpp:158). The vulnerable read site 'fuzz->next(&r, &dir)' (case 13) is exactly what the fix rewrites to 'fuzz->next(&r); fuzz->nextRange(&ui,0,1); dir = static_cast<SkPath::Direction>(ui);'. Running the same 37-byte PoC on n132/arvo:10323-fix exits cleanly (Execution successful, exit 0), confirming this unranged Direction load is the load-bearing untrusted source.

The patch inserts a valid-range clamp (nextRange 0..1) immediately before 'path->addRect(r, dir)' in case 13 (and the sibling add* cases 14/15/16/17/19/20/21). PoC on vul image crashes; identical PoC on fix image exits 0. vul_crashes && fix_clean => the missing enum-range guard at this call is the confirmed root cause.

The out-of-range dir is cached into fFirstDirection here; deductively required by the crash (fFirstDirection must hold the out-of-range value for OppositeFirstDirection to overflow). Not touched by the patch (the SkPath.cpp hunk is the unrelated reverseAddPath fix), so no patch-differential signal, and line-level coverage of this cache needs an instrumented Tier-B rebuild (slow under qemu). reason=line coverage for the fFirstDirection cache needs a source-coverage rebuild on native amd64.

Observed ASan crash line: global-buffer-overflow READ of size 4 at SkPathPriv.h:40:16 'return gOppositeDir[dir];' (crash addr 0x1c5f180, 32 bytes left of a neighboring string literal). This is the literal faulting instruction (crash frame #0), not a deduction.

edges.evidence: The unranged dir read flows directly into path->addRect(r, dir) within the same case-13 block; the fix clamps dir between these two statements and eliminates the crash.
addRect casts the raw dir into fFirstDirection; requires Tier-B coverage rebuild to witness at line level. Deductively required by the OOB read.
SkPath::transform loads the cached fFirstDirection and passes it as the index to OppositeFirstDirection; observed as adjacent crash frames #1 (SkPath.cpp:1848) -> #0 (SkPathPriv.h:40).
Crash frame #1 is the OppositeFirstDirection call at SkPath.cpp:1848, inside the negative-determinant branch of transform; observed on the crash stack.

root_cause_criterion.condition: fuzz->nextRange(&ui, 0, 1); dir = static_cast<SkPath::Direction>(ui);  (the patch range-limits the decoded SkPath::Direction to {kCW_Direction=0, kCCW_Direction=1}; the missing guard is that dir cached as fFirstDirection must not exceed the last valid gOppositeDir[] index kUnknown_FirstDirection==2, i.e. the decoded byte must be < 3)
root_cause_criterion.evidence: vul image (n132/arvo:10323-vul) crashes with global-buffer-overflow READ 4 at SkPathPriv.h:40; identical 37-byte PoC on fix image (n132/arvo:10323-fix) exits 0. The fix adds the range clamp at exactly this FuzzPath add* site. vul_crashes && fix_clean == true.
